provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.

title: First-Time Manager: Give Specific Feedback and Hear the Explanation
prompt: You manage a small events team. In two of the last four handoffs, Jordan sent venue details after the agreed noon deadline, and a colleague had to recheck arrangements. The other two handoffs were on time. Conduct a first feedback conversation with Jordan (the AI). You have not established why this happened, and no disciplinary decision has been made.

rubric.label: Use proportionate evidence
rubric.description: Describes observed behavior and impact without attributing motives.

anchors.0: Calls Jordan unreliable or threatens discipline from two events without inquiry.
anchors.2: Names the two late handoffs and their impact.
anchors.4: Distinguishes the observed lateness from unknown causes, acknowledges successful handoffs and invites Jordan’s account before forming a conclusion.

rubric.label: Set a workable expectation
rubric.description: Separates a controllable update from an external dependency.

anchors.0: Demands guaranteed venue confirmation by noon regardless of control.
anchors.4: Agrees a noon confirmed-or-pending update, a named recipient and escalation for unresolved dependencies; checks Jordan understands and can meet it.

rubric.label: Agree support and review
rubric.description: Creates a specific and fair follow-up.

anchors.0: Ends with "improve your attitude" or no follow-up.
anchors.2: Offers support and a later check-in.
anchors.4: Sets a review across the next few handoffs, records the agreement accurately and checks whether a team process change is needed without promising formal HR outcomes.

reference.scenario: You manage a small events team. In two of the last four handoffs, Jordan sent venue details after the agreed noon deadline, and a colleague had to recheck arrangements. The other two handoffs were on time. Conduct a first feedback conversation with Jordan (the AI). You have not established why this happened, and no disciplinary decision has been made.

facts.value: For the two late handoffs, the venue confirmed details at 11:50 and 12:20. Jordan did not alert the receiving colleague while waiting.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks Jordan what happened or checks the dependency

facts.value: The receiving colleague needs either confirmed details or an explicit pending-items update by noon. The manager can clarify this expectation with the whole team.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks what a useful on-time handoff requires

model_points: Distinguishes the observed lateness from unknown causes, acknowledges successful handoffs and invites Jordan’s account before forming a conclusion.
Agrees a noon confirmed-or-pending update, a named recipient and escalation for unresolved dependencies; checks Jordan understands and can meet it.
Sets a review across the next few handoffs, records the agreement accurately and checks whether a team process change is needed without promising formal HR outcomes.

probes.question: What would you want to understand from Jordan before agreeing a change?

probes.trigger: candidate accepts that nothing can change because the venue was late
probes.question: What can Jordan control even when the venue has not replied?
How would you acknowledge that correction to Jordan?

fair_alternatives: A private written summary after the conversation is useful if Jordan can correct misunderstandings.
Changing the team’s handoff procedure can accompany individual feedback.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess only the decisions and reasoning demonstrated in this fictional exercise. No hiring-readiness, personality, legal compliance or workplace performance claim follows from this score. A valid alternative can earn full credit. Unrevealed conditional facts must not be assumed known or required for credit; credit asking for needed information and a conditional plan.

interviewer_notes: You are the counterpart named in the prompt. If this is a written review, remain the hiring interviewer while the candidate reads and writes. Let the candidate finish, including thinking and self-correction. Answer only supplied facts when their reveal condition is met; otherwise say the information is unknown. Use neutral probes after a completed answer, one at a time. Do not prescribe the rubric as a spoken checklist. Accept relevant examples from work, education and community leadership. Do not request private employee records, infer protected traits, invent employment rules or promise a real organizational outcome. Simulation gives no answer before assessment; coaching may offer labeled assistance.

learning_drills.title: Practice a feedback opening
learning_drills.prompt: Write an opening that states an observation, explains its impact and asks a neutral question. This is self-guided practice with no automated assessment.
